item.title: Jake White appointed Flying Fijians coach
item.description: Alipate Narawa , Temalesi Vono · 13/10/2026 Speaking during the announcement today, White says his focus will be on creating genuine competition for every jersey and selecting players who are ready to give everything to represent Fiji.
item.content:encoded:
Alipate Narawa , Temalesi Vono · 13/10/2026

Speaking during the announcement today, White says his focus will be on creating genuine competition for every jersey and selecting players who are ready to give everything to represent Fiji.

White stresses that the Flying Fijians belong to all Fijians, not just the players and coaching staff.

He says supporters, families, villages, schools, clubs, communities and Fijians living overseas all have a role to play in the team's success.

White says every act of support and contribution will help strengthen the team as it works towards achieving greater success on the international stage.

White says he is grateful for the opportunity to lead the Flying Fijians and is determined to work with the team and the wider Fijian community to make the country proud.

He says the journey towards greater heights will require everyone to work together. White will coach the Flying Fijians as they take on Japan in a Test match next Saturday at 5.50pm.

The team will then prepare for the next round of the Nations Cup in November.

item.title: Team Fiji athletes receive hygiene packs ahead of Youth Olympic Games
item.description: Team Fiji’s young athletes will receive additional personal care support for their journey to the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, following donations of Rexona and U by Kotex hygiene packs from the Motibhai Group of Companies. The donations are aimed at supporting the comfort and wellbeing of athletes and officials, with the U by Kotex packs specifically provided for Team Fiji’s female
item.content:encoded:
Team Fiji’s young athletes will receive additional personal care support for their journey to the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, following donations of Rexona and U by Kotex hygiene packs from the Motibhai Group of Companies.

The donations are aimed at supporting the comfort and wellbeing of athletes and officials, with the U by Kotex packs specifically provided for Team Fiji’s female athletes.

Team Fiji Chef de Mission Jane Wong says the support will help athletes and officials feel comfortable, prepared and able to focus on their performances.

Wong says athlete wellbeing is an important part of performance and thanked Motibhai Group and its brands for recognising the needs of the team, including its female athletes.

Motibhai Group Marketing Manager Praneeta Devi says the company is proud to continue supporting Team Fiji as its athletes prepare to represent the country on the international stage.

Devi says supporting female athletes also aligns with the company’s commitment to health, wellbeing and youth empowerment.

The Youth Olympic Games will be held in Dakar from 30th October to 13th November , bringing together young athletes from around the world to compete across various sporting disciplines.

Motibhai Group has a long-standing partnership with Team Fiji, supporting athletes in their preparations for major international sporting events.

item.title: Five points separate top four as Skipper Cup heads into quarter-finals
item.description: Only five points separate the top four teams on the Skipper Cup Senior points table as the competition heads into the quarter-finals this Saturday. Nadi leads the standings with 45 points after 11 rounds, with Tailevu just two points behind on 43.
item.content:encoded:
Only five points separate the top four teams on the Skipper Cup Senior points table as the competition heads into the quarter-finals this Saturday.

Nadi leads the standings with 45 points after 11 rounds, with Tailevu just two points behind on 43.

Nadroga is third with 41 points, while Naitasiri is fourth with 40 points.

Defending champions Malolo sit fifth with 34 points, followed by Suva and Navosa on 29 points each, while Ba is eighth with 26 points.

These eight teams have qualified for Saturday's quarter-finals, while Taveuni, Lautoka, Kadavu and Rewa have missed out on the knockout stage.

The quarter-final matches will be played at three venues, HFC Bank Stadium in Suva, Lawaqa Park in Sigatoka and King Charles Park in Nadi.

The semi-finals are scheduled for October 24th, followed by the final on October 31st.

The venue for the final is yet to be confirmed.

item.title: FRU to announce new Flying Fijians head coach tomorrow
item.description: The Fiji Rakavi Football Union (FRU) will announce the new head coach of the FIJI Water Flying Fijians tomorrow, with the team facing a tight schedule ahead of their upcoming international fixtures. According to the advertised terms for the position, the successful candidate’s contract runs from the 5th of this month, until 31st December 2027.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Rakavi Football Union (FRU) will announce the new head coach of the FIJI Water Flying Fijians tomorrow, with the team facing a tight schedule ahead of their upcoming international fixtures.

According to the advertised terms for the position, the successful candidate’s contract runs from the 5th of this month, until 31st December 2027.

The announcement comes as the Flying Fijians prepare to face Japan on the 24th of this month before beginning their Nations Championship campaign in November.

Questions remain over when preparations under the new head coach will begin, given the limited time before the Japan Test.

The Union had earlier confirmed that it received 31 applications for the position.

Meanwhile, Shaun Edwards is no longer in contention after signing with Argentina.

Edwards is widely regarded as one of the world’s leading defence coaches.

Stay with us as we will bring you the latest update on this.

item.title: Bati must withstand pressure and take their chances against Australia – Potter
item.description: Fiji Bati Head Coach Mick Potter says his side must withstand pressure, remain resilient and make the most of every scoring opportunity if they are to compete against teams such as Australia at the Rugby League World Cup, which kicks off this Thursday. The Bati will face Australia and New Zealand in their pool matches, two of the strongest teams in international rugby league.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Bati Head Coach Mick Potter says his side must withstand pressure, remain resilient and make the most of every scoring opportunity if they are to compete against teams such as Australia at the Rugby League World Cup, which kicks off this Thursday.

The Bati will face Australia and New Zealand in their pool matches, two of the strongest teams in international rugby league.

When asked what Fiji needs to do to progress further in the tournament, Potter says Australia builds its game around applying constant pressure on the opposition.

He says the Bati must remain composed and resilient when things are not going their way and avoid conceding points under pressure.

Potter says Australia has high-quality players who will give Fiji very few opportunities to score tries.

He says when those opportunities come, the Bati must make them count.

The Bati will begin their World Cup campaign against the Cook Islands at 5.05pm this Sunday at McDonald Jones Stadium in Newcastle.

They will then face Australia at 9.05pm on the 25th of this month before taking on New Zealand at 4.30pm on the 31st.
